quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Meets our preferred position: Vendor IP indemnity covering Customer and Affiliates (20.1), plus indemnities for breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach caused by Vendor, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2). Customer's indemnity is narrow (Customer-supplied material and Customer's unlawful use, with carve-outs) (20.3), procedure is standard (20.4), and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies are in addition to defence (20.5). Indemnities sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims (21.3).

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: Direction is correct: we own Customer Data and our pre-existing IP with no transfer to Vendor beyond a service-provision processing right (14.1), we own Deliverables by assignment (14.2), Vendor retains only Vendor Technology with a perpetual licence back under 13.2 (14.3), and joint ownership and feedback assignment are excluded (14.4).
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] "Fees" is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so as drafted the mutual cap is effectively USD 12,000 — illusory. We have reset the basis to all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim, with a USD 1,000,000 floor, consistent with our standard position. Indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security and IP infringement remain outside the cap as Excluded Claims (21.3), which we accept as drafted.

ops.newText: shall not exceed the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
ops.oldText: shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim

proposal.summary: Fix cap basis: all amounts payable under the Agreement in the preceding 12 months, floored at USD 1,000,000

quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
rationale: The cap is mutual, indirect damages are mutually excluded, and the Excluded Claims definition (21.3) carves out confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, with payment obligations excluded from "damages" — all compliant. However the quantum is illusory: "Fees" is defined in 1.5/1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the cap is effectively USD 12,000 rather than 12 months' fees. Redlined to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
rationale: We may assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without consent (24.1); Vendor may not assign or transfer by change of control without our consent and never to a competitor (24.2); and 24.4 removes any Vendor right triggered by our change of control. Preferred position met.

quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us. Section 2.1 confirms we pay only for Services ordered and that declining to order is not a breach, and 12.3 preserves our right to engage any supplier.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; 15% of annual Fees per week of delay is punitive and unenforceable in most of our jurisdictions, and it also conflicts with our right to withhold disputed amounts in 7.3. We have deleted it — if a late-payment remedy is needed we can accept simple interest at a commercially reasonable rate on undisputed overdue amounts.
proposal.summary: Delete liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week payable by Customer on late payment

quote: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer at 15% of annual Fees per week of delay, which is punitive, potentially unlimited in aggregate, and inconsistent with our right to withhold disputed amounts under 7.3. Our position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; deleted, with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts offered as the fallback.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes
rationale: The grant already covers our Affiliates and contractors (13.1), paid-up/embedded licences are perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free with modification and derivative rights (13.2), and licences are transferable to Affiliates/successors and revocable only for a material uncured breach after notice and cure (13.3). Preferred position met.

quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, acquire or sell any product and to operate in any field or territory. The only competitive covenant (12.4) restricts Vendor, which is acceptable and in our favour.

quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
rationale: We have a convenience right on 30 days' notice (9.4 read with 29.4) with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination fee, and Section 9 gives Vendor no convenience right (only material breach and insolvency). This matches our preferred position.

quote: Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer.
rationale: Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems or unrelated data (22.2). Exactly our preferred position.

quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, and no mandatory arbitration (only a short good-faith executive escalation that does not delay urgent relief). This is our preferred position.

quote: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.
rationale: The only MFN runs in our favour (Vendor-granted best pricing in 7.6), and 12.3 confirms we have given no most-favoured-customer commitment. No redline required.

quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
rationale: No take-or-pay, minimum volume or shortfall exposure: 2.1 disclaims any purchase commitment, 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges, and 12.3 confirms no minimum-volume commitment. Preferred position met.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: No non-solicit or no-hire binds us; a document-wide search for "solicit" returns nothing, and 12.3 expressly confirms no no-hire commitment and preserves general-recruitment hiring. Matches our preferred position.

quote: thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
rationale: Automatic 12-month renewals with a 30-day Customer opt-out, a 60-day Vendor reminder (with deadline extension if missed), and renewal uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% on 90 days' notice — exactly our preferred position.

quote: Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
rationale: Six months' transition assistance at Order Form rates, Customer Data returned within 30 days in a documented machine-readable format with metadata and no fee-dispute holdback, and certified deletion only after we confirm successful return (11.3). Matches our preferred position, and Section 10 does not condition return on payment.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: Professional/workmanlike warranty plus a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty and term-long hosted Services conformance, with re-performance/repair/replace and a termination-and-refund backstop (19.4), plus compliance-with-law and no-malicious-code warranties (19.3). The disclaimer in 19.5 expressly does not limit the express warranties, so it does not swallow them.

quote: commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000
rationale: Section 18 meets or exceeds our preferred limits (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp), runs through the term plus one year, requires certificates on request and notice of cancellation, and confirms insurance does not cap Vendor's liability.
